plan.summary: This 1-4 block is an off-camp boxing build with strength, power, and enough conditioning to support the work using bodyweight-only training. Week 1 establishes baselines with simple assessment sessions so the main work in Weeks 2-4 can be progressed cleanly. The goal of this first block is to raise general force output, keep speed present, and build repeatable conditioning without adding unnecessary fatigue before the next 4-week review.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general lower-body and upper-body strength, simple explosive output, and repeatable conditioning with bodyweight-only methods.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress harder unilateral strength, faster plyometric work, and tighter conditioning doses while keeping recovery manageable.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength with lower volume and express it through sharper speed, jumps, throws if available, and fight-relevant conditioning.

exercises.name: 1a. Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump fast and land quietly. Reset between reps so each jump stays crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simpler jump variation with a dead start.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low safe box and step down each rep.

exercises.name: 2. Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat Assessment
exercises.notes: Warm up with bodyweight sets, then perform one hard top set per side using a 3 second lower and full range. Stop 0-1 reps before technical breakdown. Log reps and setup used so this becomes your baseline for the block.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean set per side with the same tempo and setup.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rear-foot-elevated work is uncomfortable or setup is awkward.

substitutionOptions.name: Shrimp Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if you already perform it cleanly.

exercises.name: 3a. Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Pause for 2 seconds at the top. Keep ribs down and avoid twisting.

substitutionOptions.name: Feet-Elevated Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use both legs if single-leg control is poor.

exercises.name: 3b. Side Plank
exercises.notes: Straight line from head to heel. Do not let the hips rotate back.

substitutionOptions.name: Copenhagen Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a short-lever version if you want a harder adductor emphasis.

exercises.name: 4. Tempo Squat Iso Hold
exercises.notes: Hold around parallel with full-foot pressure and upright posture. This should burn but stay technically clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Wall Sit
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if balance limits the free squat hold.

exercises.name: 5. Shadow Boxing Intervals
exercises.notes: Fast relaxed rounds. Keep footwork active and hands sharp without turning it into a grind.

endurancePrescription.format: 6 rounds of 2 minutes on, 1 minute easy walk or nose-breath recovery
endurancePrescription.progression: Keep speed and rhythm high. If breathing falls apart, shorten the work rate inside the round rather than forcing it.

exercises.name: 1a. Plyo Push-Up
exercises.notes: Explode up with clean body line. Use low-amplitude reps and stop before speed drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Release Explosive Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if leaving the floor is too aggressive.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Explosive Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a bench or sturdy surface if needed to keep speed high.

exercises.name: 2. Push-Up Assessment
exercises.notes: Warm up with a few easy sets, then perform one all-out clean set and stop when body line or range breaks. Log total reps to set your baseline for the block.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track total clean reps with the same hand position and standard each time.

substitutionOptions.name: Feet-Elevated Push-Up Assessment
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are too easy.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up Assessment
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard floor push-ups are not yet strong enough.

exercises.name: 3a. Pike Push-Up
exercises.notes: Lower under control and press through the shoulders. Keep the head moving slightly forward, not straight down.

substitutionOptions.name: Downward Dog Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if full pike push-ups are too hard.

exercises.name: 3b. Prone Y-T-W Raise
exercises.notes: Small clean reps. Squeeze between the shoulder blades and keep the neck relaxed.

exercises.name: 4. Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Low back stays flat. If needed, bend the knees slightly to keep position.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you cannot hold hollow position without arching.

exercises.name: 5. Tempo Conditioning Circuit
exercises.notes: Move steadily and breathe through the nose when possible. Keep output smooth, not frantic.

endurancePrescription.format: 4 rounds: 40 sec mountain climbers, 40 sec fast shadow boxing, 40 sec bear crawl hold or crawl, 60 sec easy walk or shakeout
endurancePrescription.progression: Add one round in Week 3 if recovery is good. Keep posture and rhythm clean.

exercises.name: 1. Doorframe or Towel Row Assessment
exercises.notes: Warm up with easier angles first, then perform one hard clean set using the strongest safe setup you have. Keep the body rigid and pull the chest toward the hands. Log the variation and reps for your baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the hardest clean row variation and reps with the same setup.

substitutionOptions.name: Table Row Assessment
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a stable heavy table if available.

substitutionOptions.name: Backpack Bent-Over Row Assessment
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if no safe bodyweight row setup exists.

exercises.name: 2a. Scap Push-Up
exercises.notes: Keep elbows straight and move only through the shoulder blades.

substitutionOptions.name: Wall Scap Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor control is limited.

exercises.name: 2b. Reverse Snow Angel
exercises.notes: Slow controlled reps. Lift the hands only as high as you can without shrugging.

exercises.name: 3a. Superman Hold
exercises.notes: Lift lightly, not maximally. Keep the glutes on and the neck neutral.

exercises.name: 3b. Cross-Body Mountain Climber
exercises.notes: Drive the knee with control and keep the shoulders stacked over the hands.

exercises.name: 4. Aerobic Flush Shadow Boxing
exercises.notes: Stay relaxed and technical. This is recovery-oriented conditioning, not hard intervals.

endurancePrescription.format: 5 rounds of 3 minutes easy-moderate with 1 minute relaxed walk
endurancePrescription.progression: Keep it conversational and finish feeling better than when you started.

exercises.name: 1a. Skater Jump to Stick
exercises.notes: Jump laterally, stick the landing, and own the position for a full second.

substitutionOptions.name: Lateral Bound to Stick
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a smaller distance if balance or landing quality is limited.

substitutionOptions.name: Lateral Step and Stick
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this lower-impact option if the landing is noisy or unstable.

exercises.name: 2. Step-Up Assessment
exercises.notes: Use a stable chair, step, or stairs setup. Warm up first, then perform one hard clean set per side with full foot contact and no push-off from the trailing leg. Log step height and reps.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the highest-quality step-up variation, height, and reps per side.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat Assessment
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you do not have a stable step.

exercises.name: 3a. Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Step back softly, stay tall through the torso, and drive up hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if balance is better with a fixed stance.

exercises.name: 3b. V-Up or Tuck-Up
exercises.notes: Move smoothly and avoid yanking through the neck.

substitutionOptions.name: Strict Leg Raise
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if V-ups are too aggressive on the low back.

exercises.name: 4. Neck Flexion and Extension Isometric
exercises.notes: Use your hands for light resistance only. Keep pressure gentle and stop if there is any discomfort.

exercises.name: 5. Repeat Sprint Circuit
exercises.notes: Work hard but keep mechanics controlled. If joints feel beat up, switch to fast shadow boxing rounds.

endurancePrescription.format: 8 rounds of 20 sec hard high-knee run in place or short shuttle, 70 sec easy walk
endurancePrescription.progression: Keep the hard efforts fast and stop one round early if speed drops sharply.
